source: Minchat Shai on Gen 48:20 (the Masorah; the Zohar named by folio)
claim_en: LEMOR ('saying') written FULL with the vav — 'this one alone is full in the Torah, and it is the first of the verse' (MS, who sends the reader to the Zohar, folio 233): the Torah's ONE full saying-word opens the living blessing-formula ('By you shall Israel bless: God make you as Ephraim and as Manasseh') — and the SAME VERSE carries the word again LEAN (idx7, asserted): one verse, one word, both spellings — the full mouth for the blessing that every generation will say, the lean for the stage direction; the Kitzur counts the vav (six) against the six places Ephraim precedes Manasseh and the six righteous judges to stand from him (named).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 48:20 (the Masorah's pair)
claim_en: YESIMKHA Elohim ('may God MAKE YOU as Ephraim and as Manasseh'): the Masorah counts TWO lean tokens of the make-you skeleton — the BLESSING here and the CURSE in Jeremiah ('May the LORD make you like Zedekiah and like Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in fire', Jer 29:22, named beyond the Torah's stream): Israel's household blessing-formula and the exiles' curse-formula share one lean skeleton — the Torah-side token checked Torah-unique in-stream.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 48:18 (the Hilleli vs the Yerushalmi; the Ramah)
claim_en: ki ze ha-BEKHOR ('for THIS is the firstborn' — Joseph's protest): the HILLELI copy writes it FULL, the YERUSHALMI copy LEAN — 'and so it is lean in all accurate books' (MS), for it is not in the Masorah's list of FOUR full firstborn-tokens in the Torah (mnemonic given at the Miketz section; the Ramah: 'all the rest are written lean') — the stream writes 48:18 LEAN with the Yerushalmi against the Hilleli, and its LEAN census is exactly FOUR (43:33 the seating by birthright; 48:18 the protest; Deut 21:16-17 the law of the hated wife's firstborn — checked); the stream's own FULL census counts six stations (41:51, 48:14, Num 3:2, Deut 15:19, 21:15, 25:6 — printed beside the Masorah's four-count, the readings named, never merged): the letter thins the firstbornship at the very verse where Joseph asserts it.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 48:7 (the Hilleli vs the Yerushalmi; the Ramah's nine)
claim_en: LAVO efrata ('to come to Ephrath' — Rachel's death-road): the HILLELI writes the come-word FULL, the YERUSHALMI LEAN — 'and so it is lean in all the books, and it is the FIRST of the nine lean ones' whose mnemonic the Masorah gives at this very verse (the Ramah lists them too): the stream's bare-skeleton census reads EIGHT lean tokens in the Torah with Rachel's road FIRST in canon order (checked; the Masorah's nine-list runs past the Torah's bare form — its further stations named by the chain, not counted here): the road-word to Bethlehem thinned at the grave Jacob is apologizing for.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 48:10 (the measure-for-measure)
claim_en: MI-ZOQEN ('from AGE' — 'and Israel's eyes were heavy from age, he could not see'): the from-age word written LEAN, its ONE Torah token (checked) — the Kitzur reads it against Isaac's dimming ('and it was when Isaac was old, his eyes dimmed from seeing', 27:1): as Jacob deceived his blind father at a blessing, so his own son crossed his sons on him at his blessing — the two dimmed-eyes blessings, measure for measure (named); and under the heavy eyes the swap this time is the SEER's own doing.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 48:9 (the unique token; Hosea named)
claim_en: QACHEM na elai ('TAKE THEM, pray, to me, and I will bless them'): the take-them word unique in the Torah (checked; 'there is none other' — the Kitzur's note), and its one Scripture-partner is Hosea's with the qamats — 'I taught Ephraim to walk, TAKING THEM on His arms' (Hos 11:3, named): the Kitzur reads the Presence taking the boys onto His arms at the hour Jacob blessed them — the grandfather's take-them answered by God's.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 48:16 (the Masorah's pair)
claim_en: ve-YIQARE vahem shemi ('and let my name BE CALLED in them'): the passive be-called form — its one Torah station by vocalization (checked by the reading-form); the Kitzur's pair is the name-called-in-Israel verse (the levirate house, Deut 25:10, named): all the tribes of Israel are called by Joseph's name, as it is said 'You redeemed with an arm Your people, the sons of Jacob AND JOSEPH, selah' (Ps 77:16, named by the Kitzur): the name asked into the lads spreads to the nation.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 48:6 (the Masorah's pair)
claim_en: al shem achehem YIQARU be-nachalatam ('by the name of their brothers THEY SHALL BE CALLED in their inheritance'): the passive they-shall-be-called — its one Torah station by vocalization (checked); the Kitzur's pair is Levi's sons (named): as Joseph's later sons are called by their brothers' tribal names in the land, so the landless tribe's sons are called through the cities of all Israel — the two called-not-counted houses paired.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 47:31-48:2 (the bed-file; Esther named)
claim_en: va-yitchazeq yisrael va-yeshev AL ha-mita ('and Israel STRENGTHENED himself and sat UPON the bed'): the upon-the-bed adjacency — its ONE Torah station (checked; 47:31 bows at the bed's HEAD, 49:33 gathers his feet INTO it: the span's bed-triple named) — and the Kitzur's file closes on Esther: the righteous, even weak, STRENGTHEN on the bed; the wicked, even in power, FALL on it ('and Haman was fallen upon the bed', Esth 7:8, named beyond the stream): the armed bed-file of gen_70 lands at its strengthening station.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 48:7/9/12/13/19 (the file; the old Sepharad codices)
claim_en: The chapter's pointing file: le-APAV ('to his face' — the bow) with the pe DAGESHED (checked); vi-SEMOLO ('at his left', 48:13) with the bet and shin SOFT; va-eqbereha SHAM ('and I buried her THERE', 48:7) with the there-word's shin DAGESHED (the pressing-together point after the buried-her verb: the grave and its there fused); yihye le-AM ('shall become a people', 48:19) lamed soft; va-AVARAKHEM ('and I will bless them', 48:9) with the kaf in TSERE — MS reporting the OLD SEPHARAD CODICES so, and the stream WRITES the tsere: the stream WITH the old codices at the blessing-word (where at 47:30 it went against them) — the file checked and asserted.

source: the stream's own census on Gen 48:14/16 (the blessing's coined verbs)
claim_en: The blessing scene coins TWO verbs found nowhere else in the Torah: ve-YIDGU ('and may they TEEM-LIKE-FISH in the midst of the land' — the fish-verb minted from the noun, its one token checked) and SIKEL et yadav ('he CROSSED his hands WISELY', 48:14 — the wise-crossing verb, its one token asserted): the scene that inverts the birth order writes its own grammar — a verb for the multiplying and a verb for the crossing, each stamped once.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 48:14 (the letter-count; Joshua)
claim_en: ve-hu ha-TZAIR ('and he was the YOUNGER'): the definite younger-word — its ONE Torah token (checked), planted at the very verse where the hands cross toward him; the Kitzur's count reads it 'he made himself SMALL' — and for that self-smallness Joshua, full of wisdom, goes out from him (named): the younger who did not claim the right hand receives it.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 48:5/19/22 (named-only)
claim_en: The Kitzur's number-crowns, carried NAMED-ONLY (letter-arithmetic, not stream-marks): EFRAYIM u-MENASHE ('Ephraim and Manasseh') = REUVEN ve-SHIMON ('Reuben and Simeon') by letter-count — the equivalence Jacob DECLARES ('as Reuben and Simeon they shall be mine') is exact in the letters' own arithmetic; YADATI ('I know', 48:19) = 'five kings' by count (five kings to go out from Manasseh); ve-zaro yihye MELO ('and his seed shall be the FULLNESS') = JOSHUA by count — the fullness-of-nations named as the man; SHEKHEM ACHAD ('one portion', 48:22) = 'the firstborn's share' by count — and the portion-word is the town's name: the plot bought at Shechem where Joseph's own bones will rest (Josh 24:32, named): the stations checked, the arithmetic named.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 97:5
claim_en: THE CROSSED HANDS ARE VERIFIED AS A STANDING PRECEDENCE, AND THE TORAH MEMBERS OF THE CENSUS HOLD. From 48:20's 'he set Ephraim before Manasseh' the chain builds a nine-item census of the younger standing first ever after - in genealogies, in the census lineage, in inheritance, in the banners, in the princes' offerings, in judges, in kings, and in the blessing formula itself. GRADED LEG BY LEG. THE TORAH LEGS ARE CONFIRMED at all three of their seats: the lineage lists Ephraim at Numbers 1:32 before Manasseh at 1:34; the banners place Ephraim's standard at 2:18 with Manasseh set beside him at 2:20; and the princes' offerings give Ephraim THE SEVENTH DAY (7:48) and Manasseh THE EIGHTH (7:54). THE REMAINING LEGS ARE DECLARED UNOPENED - inheritance, judges and kings lie in books outside this Torah-only corpus. Three confirmed, the rest named as unreached, and no grade borrowed between them.

source: Onkelos Genesis 48:22; Bereshit Rabbah 99:7
claim_en: THE PATRIARCH IS DISARMED BY BOTH MEMBERS OF THE READING, INDEPENDENTLY. 'Which I took from the hand of the Amorite WITH MY SWORD AND WITH MY BOW' is rendered by Onkelos 'with MY PRAYER ‹צלותי› and with MY PLEA ‹בעותי›' - the weapons removed from his hands altogether. And the chain arrives at the same place from its own direction, ruling that the sword is not his at all: it is Esau's, its title traced to the blessing of 27:40. Two witnesses disarm one verse by two different methods - the translation by substituting the instruments, the midrash by reassigning their ownership. The sweep's cleanest double witness, and the unit's conquest operator carries neither weapon.

check.note: A verse's weapons removed by the translation through substitution and by the chain through reassignment of ownership, independently.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 97:2; Onkelos Genesis 48:15
claim_en: THE DIRECTION OF DEPENDENCE IS ARGUED OFF ONE PREPOSITION, AND THE TRANSLATION VOTES. 'The God before whom my fathers WALKED' is read two ways: R. Yohanan sees a SHEPHERD standing while the flock walks before him - so the walking is for our sake and we need His glory; Reish Lakish sees a KING walking with the ELDERS BEFORE HIM in procession - so the walking is honor paid and, as the passage puts it, He needs our glory. Onkelos settles it in Reish Lakish's direction twice over, rendering the walking as SERVED and the shepherding as SUSTAINED. A dispute about which way dependence runs between God and the patriarchs, decided in translation against one of the two named opinions - and this corpus records the losing opinion too.

check.note: A two-way dispute over the direction of dependence, resolved by the translation in one named authority's favour, both readings preserved.

source: Onkelos Genesis 48:14
claim_en: THE TRANSLATION DOES NOT RENDER THE DIFFICULT VERB - IT STATES THE INTENT AND THE REASON. 'He GUIDED HIS HANDS KNOWINGLY' becomes 'he placed his hands SO DELIBERATELY, EVEN THOUGH MANASSEH WAS THE FIRSTBORN.' The crossing is declared purposeful inside the text itself, with the objection pre-answered in the same clause - which is exactly what the precedence census then confirms across the later books. Where the Hebrew leaves a reader to infer the intent from the outcome, the buffer supplies it as a fact about the act.

check.note: An obscure verb replaced by a statement of the actor's intent and the objection to it, making a crossing deliberate in the text.

source: Onkelos Genesis 48:21
claim_en: THE BUFFER'S STANDING FORMULA FOR DIVINE ACCOMPANIMENT, AT ITS SECOND OF THREE SEATS. 'God will be WITH YOU and bring you back' becomes 'the WORD ‹מימרא› ('memra') of God will be YOUR SUPPORT.' This sweep has now recorded the identical construction at three places in the Joseph cycle - in the prison house, here at the adoption, and in Joseph's own blessing in the next block. A consistent policy rather than a local choice: divine presence is stated as the Word's support, never as bare accompaniment.

check.note: A single formula for divine accompaniment held at three separate seats across one narrative cycle.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 97:1
claim_en: THE BLESSING IS SUSPECTED OF FAVOURITISM AT THE MOMENT IT IS GIVEN. When Joseph came out from the blessing with his face glowing, the brothers said: everyone attaches himself to the successful one - he blesses him because he is king. The father answers with 'fear the LORD, His holy ones, for those who fear Him lack nothing.' The same suspicion the coat drew at the start of the cycle, aimed now at the deathbed, and recorded as the brothers' own state rather than as narration. The corpus keeps the accusation on the record beside the blessing it doubts.

check.note: A deathbed blessing recorded as suspected of favouritism by its witnesses, the suspicion preserved as their stated position.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 82:4
claim_en: A PROMISE MADE THIRTEEN CHAPTERS EARLIER IS QUOTED BACK AND CASHED IN CONSECUTIVE VERSES. The standing reading parses the Almighty's blessing as 'a NATION' meaning Benjamin and 'an ASSEMBLY OF NATIONS' meaning Manasseh and Ephraim. At 48:4 the patriarch quotes that very promise back, and at 48:5 he cashes it by adopting the two - so the grammar of a blessing given at Bethel becomes the legal warrant for an adoption at a deathbed. The credit was recorded at its own block naming this one as where it lands.

check.note: A blessing's plural phrasing parsed at an earlier block and used here as the warrant for adopting two grandsons, quoted and executed in consecutive verses.
